mainTopic: Loans and שביעית (10-year loans, conditions against שמיטה, the thirty-day rule), followed by rulings of רב about a neck-hole on שבת and wine-colored water in a מקוה.
overview: This amud opens by finishing שמואל's ruling, which רב יהודה reports in his name: שביעית cancels even a 10-year loan, because the loan will eventually reach 'לא יגש'. רב כהנא challenges this from our משנה about עדים זוממין, who pay only the value of the time and not the whole loan. רבא answers that the משנה is about a loan with a משכון, or one whose documents were handed to בית דין, and שביעית never cancels those. In a second version (איכא דאמרי), שמואל rules the opposite, and the same משנה and the same answer of רבא appear again. Next, שמואל rules that a condition saying 'שביעית will not cancel my loan' does not work. The גמרא explains this by the wording of the condition: a person may give up his own money claim, as with אונאה, but he cannot cancel a law of the תורה. The גמרא then teaches that a loan with no set due date cannot be called in for thirty days, whether it was made with a שטר or by word of mouth. That rule is learned from the extra words 'שנת השמיטה'. Finally come two rulings of רב: one about opening a garment's neck-hole on שבת, and one about wine-colored water falling into a מקוה. Each is challenged and defended, and the discussion of the מקוה continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The reason a 10-year loan is still cancelled by שביעית
steps.stepSummary: This line finishes שמואל's ruling that שביעית cancels a 10-year loan. The prohibition 'לא יגש' does not apply yet, but it eventually will.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though right now we cannot apply 'He shall not demand it' to this loan, it will eventually reach the point where 'He shall not demand it' applies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the reason behind שמואל's ruling that שביעית cancels a loan given for ten years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prohibition 'לא יגש' (do not demand payment) normally applies only once a debt is due. A 10-year loan is not due during the שמיטה year, so the prohibition does not apply right now. Still, שמואל holds that the loan is cancelled, because it will eventually reach the point of being demanded.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall not demand it'. This is the Torah's ban on demanding payment of a debt after שמיטה.
The seventh (שמיטה) year, which cancels debts.
It will eventually come to. The situation will end up there.
We 'read' it about him. The verse applies to this case.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In this first version, שמואל says the 10-year loan IS cancelled. In the איכא דאמרי version (step 5), he says it is NOT cancelled.

phrases.english: And even though now
phrases.notes: 'Now' means during the שמיטה year, before the 10-year loan is due.

phrases.english: we do not read concerning him 'He shall not demand it,'
ultimately he comes to 'He shall not demand it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּהַשְׁתָּא לָא קָרֵינַן בֵּיהּ ״לֹא יִגֹּשׂ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes שמואל's ruling, which began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שביעית cancels a loan given for ten years, because it will eventually reach the stage of 'לא יגש'.

steps.title: Challenge from our משנה: the lying witnesses would owe the whole sum
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא points out that our משנה makes the עדים זוממין pay only the value of the time. If שביעית cancels a 10-year loan, they should pay the full thousand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objected from the משנה: 'We estimate how much a person would pay to keep a thousand זוז in his hands, comparing having to repay within thirty days with having to repay within ten years.' But if you say שביעית cancels the 10-year loan, they should have to pay him the entire amount!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges שמואל's ruling by quoting our משנה about witnesses who lied about a loan's due date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the lying witnesses pay only the difference in value between a 30-day loan and a 10-year loan. But if שביעית would cancel the real 10-year loan, the borrower would never have had to repay at all. Their false testimony (30 days, before שמיטה) would then have made him lose the whole thousand, so they should pay all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: We estimate. בית דין assesses a value.
Cancels it. Releases the debt.
A silver coin.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
We estimate how much a person would want to give
so that he could have a thousand zuz in his hand,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִיתֵּן מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: comparing having to pay it back from now until thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לִיתֵּן מִכָּאן וְעַד עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: with having to pay it back from now until ten years.
And if you say that שביעית cancels it,
they should also need to pay him all of it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that שביעית cancels a 10-year loan.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under שמואל's ruling, the real loan would have been cancelled, so the lying witnesses caused a loss of the whole sum. Yet the משנה has them pay only the value of the time.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה is about loans שביעית does not cancel
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה is talking about a loan secured by a משכון, or one whose documents were handed to בית דין. שביעית does not cancel either of these.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What case are we dealing with here? One who lends on a משכון, or one who hands his loan documents over to בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends שמואל by limiting the משנה to special loans that שמיטה never cancels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not reject שמואל's rule. He says the משנה's case is one where the loan would survive שביעית anyway. In that case, the borrower would really have owed the money after ten years, so the witnesses only took away the extra time, and paying the value of the time is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What are we dealing with here?' This phrase sets up an answer that narrows the case.
An item held as security for a loan.
Hands his loan documents over to the court to collect.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What are we dealing with here?
With one who lends on a pledge,
and with one who hands his documents over to the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה is placed in a special situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about a regular 10-year loan, which שמואל says שביעית cancels.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a loan with a משכון or one handed to בית דין. These are not cancelled, so only the value of the time is owed.

steps.title: Source: the משנה in שביעית that these loans are not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs up his answer with a משנה stating that loans on a משכון, and loans whose documents were handed to בית דין, are not cancelled by שמיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One who lends on a משכון, and one who hands his documents to בית דין, these loans are not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that proves the two cases in רבא's answer really are not cancelled by שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer only works if these two kinds of loans survive שמיטה. This משנה states exactly that, so the answer to רב כהנא stands.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not cancelled by שמיטה.

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, שמואל holds that שביעית cancels a 10-year loan. Our משנה is explained as dealing with a loan secured by a משכון or one handed to בית דין, which are never cancelled.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One who lends on a pledge,
and one who hands his documents over to the court,
these loans are not cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the two cases in רבא's answer are not cancelled by שביעית.

steps.title: Second version: שמואל rules a 10-year loan is not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: In another version, שמואל rules the opposite: שביעית does not cancel a 10-year loan, because right now 'לא יגש' does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: One who lends to his friend for ten years, שביעית does not cancel it. Even though it will eventually reach 'He shall not demand it', right now, at least, we cannot apply 'He shall not demand it' to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of שמואל's statement, which reaches the opposite ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree on the facts: the debt is not due during שמיטה, but it will be later. The first version looks at the future and says it is cancelled. This version looks at the present moment of שמיטה and says it is not. Under this version, רב כהנא's challenge never comes up, because our משנה fits a regular 10-year loan.

keyTerms.meaning: At least, in any case.
Now. Here it means at the time of שמיטה.

steps.whyThisMatters: The disagreement between the two versions turns on whether שמיטה depends on the debt's status at the moment of שמיטה, or on where the debt will end up.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
One who lends to his friend for ten years,
the Sabbatical Year does not cancel it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּאָתֵי לִידֵי ״לֹא יִגֹּשׂ״,
phrases.english: And even though he will come to 'He shall not demand it,'

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא לָא קָרֵינַן בֵּיהּ ״לֹא יִגֹּשׂ״.
phrases.english: now, at least, we do not read concerning him 'He shall not demand it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposite version of the ruling in step 1, replacing the whole discussion in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שביעית does not cancel a loan given for ten years, since 'לא יגש' does not apply at the time of שמיטה.

steps.title: Support for the second version from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings support from our משנה that שביעית does not cancel a 10-year loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Our משנה teaches this too. The court estimates how much a person would pay to hold a thousand זוז, comparing paying back in thirty days with paying back in ten years. If שביעית cancelled a 10-year loan, the false witnesses would have to pay the whole thousand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא uses our משנה to support the second version of שמואל: שביעית does not cancel a 10-year loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב כהנא used this same משנה as a challenge. Here it works as a support. The false witnesses pay only the value of the extra time, not the whole loan. That suggests the loan was never cancelled by שביעית, which fits this version of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (a support from a known source)
The court estimates
A thousand זוז (the loan amount in the משנה)
Cancels it (the debt)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
We too have also learned this:
phrases.notes: In this version, the same משנה is used to back up שמואל instead of challenging him.

phrases.english: We estimate how much a person would want to give
so that a thousand zuz will be in his hand,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִיתֵּן מִכָּאן וְעַד שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: whether to give it back from now until thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לִיתֵּן מִכָּאן וְעַד עֶשֶׂר שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: or to give it back from now until ten years.
And if you say that the seventh year cancels it,
they would also need to pay him all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the second version of שמואל given in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's second version: שביעית does not cancel a 10-year loan.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה: the עדים זוממין pay only the value of the time, not the whole thousand.

steps.title: רבא rejects the proof: the משנה's loan is one that is never cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה may be talking about a loan with a משכון, or one whose documents were handed to בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What case are we dealing with? A loan given on a משכון, or a loan whose documents were handed to בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes away רב כהנא's proof by saying the משנה is about a special kind of loan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two kinds of loans are not cancelled by שביעית in any case. So the משנה's ruling tells us nothing about an ordinary 10-year loan. The proof for this version of שמואל falls away, just as the challenge fell away in the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? (limits a source to a specific case)
One who lends against collateral
One who hands his loan documents to the court

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same answer רבא gave in step 3. Here it has a different job: before it answered a challenge, and now it rejects a proof.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What are we dealing with here?
With one who lends on collateral,
and with one who hands his loan documents to the court,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה, not שמואל's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה may be talking about loans that שביעית never cancels, so it proves nothing about ordinary loans.

steps.title: משנה source: collateral loans and court-held documents are not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: רבא backs up his case limitation with a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one who lends on a משכון, and one who hands his documents to בית דין, are not cancelled by שמיטה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes a משנה to show that these two kinds of loans really are not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה makes רבא's case limitation solid. It is not just a guess. It is a known rule that these loans survive שביעית. So our משנה about עדים זוממין can fit either version of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not cancelled (by שמיטה)
Collateral, a pledge
Loan documents

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions, the משנה about עדים זוממין does not settle the question, because it can be about a loan with a משכון or one handed to בית דין.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
One who lends on collateral,
and one who hands his documents to the court,
they are not cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's limitation in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Loans with a משכון, or whose documents were handed to בית דין, are not cancelled by שביעית.

steps.title: שמואל: a condition that שביעית will not cancel a loan does not work
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that even if a lender sets a condition that שביעית will not cancel his loan, שביעית still cancels it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: If someone says to his friend, "On condition that שביעית will not cancel my loan," שביעית still cancels it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a ruling by שמואל about a lender who tries to make a condition to protect his loan from שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lender tries to make a deal ahead of time so the loan survives שביעית. שמואל says the deal does not help, and the loan is still cancelled. The גמרא will now ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: On condition that
Will cancel my debt
Cancels (the debt)

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
One who says to his fellow:
"On condition that the seventh year will not cancel my loan,"
the seventh year cancels it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about שביעית: conditions made on a loan.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition that שביעית will not cancel a loan does not work, and שביעית cancels it anyway.

steps.title: Suggested reason: a condition against the Torah is void
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל's reason is that this condition goes against what is written in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say שמואל holds that this lender is making a condition against what is written in the תורה, and anyone who makes such a condition has a void condition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason for שמואל's ruling. This suggestion sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a condition against the תורה is void. The גמרא proposes that this is why the lender's condition fails. Starting with "לימא" signals that the גמרא may soon reject this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion that is often rejected)
He holds
Making a condition against what the תורה says
His condition is void

phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel holds:

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֶה עַל מָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא,
phrases.english: He is making a condition against what is written in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה –
phrases.english: and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests a reason for the ruling in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is שמואל's reason that a condition against the תורה is void?

steps.title: Challenge: שמואל allows a condition that waives overcharging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion: in the case of אונאה, שמואל holds that such a condition does work.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was stated: if someone says to his friend, "On condition that you have no claim of אונאה against me," רב says he still has the claim, and שמואל says he has no claim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested reason by bringing a case where שמואל lets a condition override a תורה law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אונאה, the ban on overcharging, is also a תורה law, yet שמואל says a condition waiving it works. So שמואל does not seem to hold that every condition against the תורה is void, at least in money matters. Then why does the condition fail in the case of שביעית?

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so? (opens a challenge)
Overcharging or underpaying beyond the fair price, which the תורה forbids
He has a claim against him

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a basic question: when can people make money conditions that change what the תורה says? The answer will explain what is special about שביעית.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated:
One who says to his fellow:
"On condition that you have no claim of overcharging against me,"

phrases.aramaic: רַב אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לוֹ עָלָיו אוֹנָאָה,
phrases.english: Rav says: He does have a claim of overcharging against him,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אוֹמֵר: אֵין לוֹ עָלָיו אוֹנָאָה.
phrases.english: and Shmuel says: He has no claim of overcharging against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason suggested in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that שמואל holds every condition against the תורה is void.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל lets a condition waive אונאה, which is a תורה law. So he cannot hold that such conditions are always void, and his ruling on שביעית needs a different reason.

steps.title: שמואל's own explanation: it depends on how the condition is worded
steps.stepSummary: רב ענן reports that שמואל explained that a condition can remove the buyer's claim of אונאה, but it cannot remove the law of אונאה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't it already said about this ruling that רב ענן said: שמואל explained it to me himself. If the seller says, 'On condition that you have no claim of אונאה against me,' the buyer has no claim. But if he says, 'On condition that there is no אונאה in this sale,' there is still אונאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. שמואל's ruling about אונאה only works when the condition is worded in a specific way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of condition. 'You have no claim against me' asks the buyer to give up money he is owed, and a person may give up his own money. 'There is no אונאה here' tries to cancel the תורה's law, and that does not work. So the אונאה case does not contradict the idea that a condition against the תורה fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Overcharging or underpaying in a sale, which the תורה forbids
On condition that
It was explained (to me)

steps.confusionAlert: The two conditions sound almost the same, but they are not. One gives up a personal money claim and works. The other tries to cancel the law itself and fails.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about that ruling,
Rav Anan said:
It was explained to me personally by Shmuel himself:
If the seller says, "On condition that you have no claim of overcharging against me":
then the buyer has no overcharging claim against him.
If he says, "On condition that there is no overcharging in this sale":
then there is still overcharging in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by showing that שמואל's ruling on אונאה depends on how the condition is worded.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case by wording: giving up a personal claim versus cancelling the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל lets a condition cancel אונאה, so he must allow conditions that go against the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל only allows a condition that gives up a personal money claim. A condition that cancels the law itself does not work.

steps.title: The same distinction applied to שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A condition worded as the borrower giving up his right under שביעית works. A condition worded as 'שביעית will not cancel the loan' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: if the lender says, 'On condition that you will not cancel my debt in שביעית,' שביעית does not cancel it. If he says, 'On condition that שביעית will not cancel my debt,' שביעית does cancel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies שמואל's distinction from אונאה to שמואל's ruling about שביעית in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the condition is about the borrower ('you won't cancel me'), the borrower is giving up a right that belongs to him, so it works. When the condition is about the law ('שביעית won't cancel'), it tries to cancel the תורה, so it fails. This shows that step 10's reasoning was correct, and step 9 refers to the second wording.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, which cancels debts
Cancels it (the debt)
Here too, meaning the same logic applies

steps.whatToRemember: A condition can give up a person's own money right, but it cannot cancel what the תורה says. This applies both to אונאה and to שביעית.

phrases.english: Here too:
If he says, "On condition that you will not cancel my debt in the seventh year":
phrases.notes: The word "you" is the borrower, so the borrower is giving up his own right.

phrases.english: then the seventh year does not cancel it.
If he says, "On condition that the seventh year will not cancel my debt":
then the seventh year does cancel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the distinction about wording from step 12 and applies it to the case of שביעית.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's rule in step 9 refers to a condition that tries to cancel the law of שביעית. A condition in which the borrower gives up his own right does work.

steps.title: A loan with no set due date cannot be called in for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A teaching states that if someone lends without setting a time, he may not demand payment before thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: if someone lends to his friend without saying when it is due, he may not demand payment until thirty days have passed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic about loans. It brings a teaching about how long a lender must wait when no due date was set.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when no deadline was mentioned, the law gives every loan a minimum length of thirty days. The next steps ask whether this applies to every kind of loan.

keyTerms.meaning: Without saying, meaning with no due date set
Permitted
To demand payment from him

phrases.english: It was taught:
One who lends to his fellow without setting a time
is not permitted to demand payment from him
before thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about loans, following the discussion of loans and שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A loan with no set due date cannot be collected before thirty days.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה suggests the rule applies only to a loan with a שטר
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה thought the thirty-day rule applies only to a loan with a שטר, because people do not bother writing a שטר for a shorter loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה, sitting before רב, wanted to say: this rule is only for a loan with a שטר, because people don't go to the trouble of writing a שטר for less than thirty days. But a loan made by word of mouth does not get thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה suggests a limit on the teaching from step 14. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reasoning is about what people normally do. Writing a שטר takes effort, so a loan with a שטר is assumed to be for at least thirty days. A loan by word of mouth takes no effort, so it might be meant for a short time.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan with a written document
A loan made by word of mouth, with no document
These words apply (only to...)
Goes to the trouble

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב לְמֵימַר:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana, sitting before Rav, thought to say:
This applies only to a loan with a document,
because a person does not go to the trouble
of writing a document for less than thirty days.
But a loan by word of mouth does not get this rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חַנָּה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests limiting the thirty-day rule from step 14 to loans with a שטר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A suggestion that the thirty-day rule applies only to a loan with a שטר and not to a loan by word of mouth.

steps.title: רב rejects the limit: both kinds of loan get thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רב quotes his uncle, who said the thirty-day rule applies both to a loan with a שטר and to a loan by word of mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to him: this is what my uncle said: the rule is the same for someone who lends with a שטר and someone who lends by word of mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב pushes back against רבה בר בר חנה's suggestion and says the rule has no such limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב quotes his uncle (רבי חייא) to show that the thirty-day minimum applies to every loan with no set due date. The amount of effort it took to make the loan does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: My uncle (literally, my beloved one), meaning רבי חייא
Both this one... and that one

phrases.english: Rav said to him:
This is what my uncle said:
phrases.notes: "My beloved" is how רב refers to his uncle, רבי חייא.

phrases.english: It is the same for one who lends with a document
and for one who lends by word of mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב: הָכִי אָמַר חֲבִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the limit suggested in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that only a loan with a שטר gets thirty days
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to the tradition from רב's uncle, the rule covers every loan, even one by word of mouth.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא openly says the thirty-day rule applies to both a loan with a שטר and a loan by word of mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: if someone lends to his friend without a set time, he may not demand payment before thirty days. This is true both for a loan with a שטר and for a loan by word of mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רב's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא repeats the thirty-day rule and adds in plain words that it covers both kinds of loan. This settles the matter against the limit suggested in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: Thirty days, the minimum length of a loan with no set due date

steps.whatToRemember: Any loan with no set due date, whether made with a שטר or by word of mouth, cannot be called in before thirty days.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who lends to his fellow without setting a time

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְתוֹבְעוֹ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: is not permitted to demand payment from him before thirty days,
the same for one who lends with a document
and for one who lends by word of mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב's position in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that the thirty-day rule covers both kinds of loan
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that names both a loan with a שטר and a loan by word of mouth

steps.title: שמואל demands the source of the thirty-day rule
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רב מתנה to explain right away where the thirty-day loan rule comes from, for loans with a שטר and loans by word of mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב מתנה: Don't even sit down until you explain this teaching. Where do we learn what the Rabbis said, that someone who lends without setting a time cannot demand payment before thirty days, whether the loan was with a שטר or by word of mouth?
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל asks רב מתנה for the source of the thirty-day rule that was just proven in the earlier steps. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only knew that the rule exists and that it covers both kinds of loans. Now the גמרא wants to know where the rule comes from. Saying 'don't sit down until you explain it' shows how much שמואל wanted the answer right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't sit on your feet: don't sit down yet, explain it right now
A teaching or ruling
Without saying when, with no set due date
By word of mouth, with no written document

phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Mattana:
Do not sit down on your feet
phrases.notes: An expression meaning: don't relax yet, answer me right now.

phrases.english: until you explain this teaching:
From where do we know this matter that the Rabbis said:
One who lends to his fellow without setting a time

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְתוֹבְעוֹ פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם,
phrases.english: may not demand payment from him before thirty days,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד הַמַּלְוֶה בִּשְׁטָר וְאֶחָד הַמַּלְוֶה עַל פֶּה?
phrases.english: whether he lends with a document or lends by word of mouth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the rule's scope is settled, the גמרא asks for its source in the פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the thirty-day rule on loans with no set time.

steps.title: The extra words 'year of release' teach a second, shorter release
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה learns the thirty-day rule from the seemingly extra words 'שנת השמיטה'. Thirty days count as a 'year.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered: The פסוק says, 'The seventh year, the year of release, is near.' Once it says 'the seventh year is near,' don't I already know it is the שמיטה year? So why add 'the year of release'? To teach that there is another 'release' like this one. Which one? A loan with no set time, which cannot be collected before thirty days. As the Master said: thirty days within a year count as a year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers שמואל's question with a פסוק about שמיטה. He uses words that look extra to find a second kind of 'release' from collecting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The seventh year' already means שמיטה, so 'the year of release' must be teaching something new: a different period when a lender can't collect. That period is the first thirty days of an open-ended loan. It can be called a 'year' because of the rule that thirty days within a year count as a year.

keyTerms.meaning: The year of release, when loans may not be collected
Why does the פסוק need to say this? Used when words seem extra
Thirty days within a year count as a full year

steps.whatToRemember: The thirty-day rule comes from the extra words 'שנת השמיטה'. The first thirty days of an open-ended loan are a small 'שמיטה' when the lender can't collect.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it is written:
"The seventh year, the year of release, is near,"
From the fact that it says "the seventh year is near,"
don't I already know that it is the year of release?
So why does the verse say "the year of release"?

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר לָךְ: [יֵשׁ] שְׁמִטָּה אַחֶרֶת שֶׁהִיא כָּזוֹ,
phrases.english: To tell you: there is another release that is like this one,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in square brackets; it belongs to the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזוֹ – זוֹ הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ סְתָם,
phrases.english: and which is it? This is one who lends to his fellow without setting a time,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְתוֹבְעוֹ בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם.
phrases.english: who may not demand payment from him in less than thirty days.
As the Master said:
Thirty days in a year count as a year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question with a derivation from a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra phrase 'שנת השמיטה' teaches a second 'release': the first thirty days of an open-ended loan. Thirty days count as a 'year.'

steps.title: Opening a new neck-hole in a garment on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: someone who opens a garment's neck-hole on שבת is חייב חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Someone who opens the neck-hole of a garment on שבת must bring a חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new ruling by רב: opening the neck-hole of a garment on שבת is a real מלאכה, so one who does it by mistake brings a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new topic, not tied to the loan discussion. The case is a new garment whose neck opening was never cut open. Opening it makes the garment ready to wear, and the חטאת liability shows that this counts as full מלאכה. The next step will challenge it.

keyTerms.meaning: The neck opening of a garment
Must bring a sin-offering, the sign of a full Torah-level מלאכה done by mistake

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
One who opens the neck-hole of a garment on Shabbat
is liable to bring a sin-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ruling from the same pair, רב יהודה quoting רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening a garment's neck-hole on שבת is a full מלאכה, so one who does it by mistake is חייב חטאת.

steps.title: Why is this different from piercing a barrel stopper?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asks how the neck-hole differs from a barrel stopper, which may be opened on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא challenged it: What is the difference between this and the stopper of a barrel?
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges רב's ruling by comparing it to opening the stopper of a barrel on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Opening a barrel's stopper is allowed on שבת. In both cases you open something closed to make it usable, so רב כהנא asks why the neck-hole should be a serious מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenged it: raises a strong objection to a ruling
The stopper sealing a barrel
What is the difference between this and...?

phrases.english: Rav Kahana challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לִמְגוּפַת חָבִית?
phrases.english: But what is the difference between this and the stopper of a barrel?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לָהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that opening a neck-hole is חייב חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Opening a barrel stopper is allowed, and it is just as much 'opening something closed,' so the neck-hole should be no worse.

steps.title: The neck cloth is part of the garment, the stopper is not
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the cloth closing the neck-hole is part of the garment, but a stopper is a separate thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: He answered him: This one is attached, and that one is not attached.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloth closing the neck-hole is woven into the garment itself, so cutting it open finishes making the garment, which is a real מלאכה. A stopper is a separate piece meant to be taken out, so opening it doesn't make anything new.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached, a real part of the item

phrases.english: He said to him: This one is attached,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the garment's neck cloth.

phrases.english: and that one is not attached.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: זֶה חִבּוּר, וְזֶה אֵינוֹ חִבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge and defends רב's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any opening of something closed is the same, so the neck-hole should be like the stopper.
steps.terutzMaskana: The neck cloth is part of the garment, so opening it finishes the item. The stopper is separate, so opening it does not.

steps.title: Water colored by a drop of wine does not disqualify a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: three לוגין of water that look like wine because of a קורטוב of wine do not disqualify a מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Three לוגין of water into which a קורטוב of wine fell, so that they now look like wine, and that mixture fell into a מקוה: it does not disqualify the מקוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ruling from רב, this time about a מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally three לוגין of drawn water can disqualify a מקוה that does not yet hold enough water. Here a tiny bit of wine has made the water look like wine. רב rules that the mixture counts as wine, not water, so it does not disqualify the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A small unit of liquid measure
A tiny amount, one sixty-fourth of a לוג
A ritual bath
Made it invalid

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the wine 'cancels out' the water. The point is that because the mixture looks like wine, it is treated as wine, and wine does not disqualify a מקוה the way drawn water does.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Three log of water
into which a kortov of wine fell,
and they look like wine,
and they fell into a ritual bath: they do not disqualify it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another new ruling from רב יהודה quoting רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three לוגין of water that look like wine because of a קורטוב of wine do not disqualify a מקוה.

steps.title: Why is this different from dye water?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא compares the case to dye water, which רבי יוסי says does disqualify a מקוה at three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא challenged it: What is the difference between this and dye water? As we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי says dye water disqualifies a מקוה at three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges רב's מקוה ruling using a משנה about dye water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dye water is also water that has changed color, and רבי יוסי still says it disqualifies a מקוה at three לוגין. So why shouldn't water colored by wine disqualify it too?

keyTerms.meaning: Dye water, water with dye mixed into it
Make invalid

phrases.english: Rav Kahana challenged it:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לְמֵי צֶבַע?
phrases.english: But what is the difference between this and dye water?
As we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: מֵי צֶבַע פּוֹסְלִין אֶת הַמִּקְוֶה בִּשְׁלֹשֶׁת לוּגִּין.
phrases.english: Dye water disqualifies a ritual bath at three log.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לָהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא: וְכִי מָה בֵּין זֶה לְמֵי צֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that water colored like wine does not disqualify a מקוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dye water has also changed color and still disqualifies, so a change of color should not save this water either.

steps.title: Dye water is still 'water,' but this is 'diluted wine'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that dye water is still called water, but water colored by wine is called diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: There it is called 'dye water.' Here it is called 'diluted wine.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב כהנא by showing how differently people name the two mixtures.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is what the mixture is called. Dye water is still 'water,' just colored, so it disqualifies like water. Water that looks like wine is called 'diluted wine,' so it counts as wine and does not disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: Is called
Diluted wine, wine mixed with water
Dye water

steps.whatToRemember: Both rulings of רב hold up. A neck-hole is different from a stopper because the cloth is attached to the garment. Wine-colored water is different from dye water because it is called 'diluted wine,' not 'water.'

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
There, it is called "dye water,"
here, it is called "diluted wine."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge and defends רב's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by what the mixture is called
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any colored water is still water, so it should disqualify like dye water.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dye water keeps the name 'water.' Wine-colored water is called 'diluted wine,' so it counts as wine and does not disqualify.

steps.title: רבי חייא taught that this water does disqualify the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a teaching of רבי חייא saying that three לוגין of water with a קורטוב of wine in it 'bring down' (disqualify) the מקוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חייא teach: they disqualify the מקוה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's ruling from step 23. It quotes רבי חייא, who taught the opposite: this wine-colored water does ruin the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25, רבא explained רב with logic: water colored by wine is called diluted wine, not water. Now there is a direct source, רבי חייא's teaching, that rules the opposite about the very same case. The question is no longer about logic but about a source that contradicts רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'they brought down the מקוה': they make it invalid for טבילה
A ritual bath used for טבילה
A tiny measure of liquid; here, a small amount of wine that colors the water
Invalid, not fit for use

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥiyya teach:
They disqualify the ritual bath!
phrases.notes: 'They' means the three לוגין of water with the bit of wine in it, the same case רב spoke about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא defended רב's ruling with logic in step 25, the גמרא now brings a teaching that says the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling (step 23) that three לוגין of wine-colored water do not disqualify a מקוה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא's teaching rules directly on the same case and says the water does disqualify the מקוה, which contradicts רב.

steps.title: רבא says each ruling follows a different side of an argument
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that there is no contradiction: רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and רבי חייא's teaching follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not difficult. This one follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and that one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the clash between רב and רבי חייא. He says they are not really arguing with each other; each one is following a different older opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of saying one source is wrong, רבא shows that the question was already argued about earlier. רב sides with רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who looks at the water's color, so wine-colored water counts as wine. רבי חייא sides with the רבנן, who still count it as drawn water that ruins the מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult': the contradiction can be solved
'This one... that one': assigning each source to a different opinion
The Sages, the majority opinion that argues with a single named sage
A disagreement between sages

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying רב or רבי חייא made a mistake. He is saying each one follows a real earlier opinion, so both teachings are correct within their own view.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is not difficult,
this ruling follows Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri,
that one follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: 'That' is רבי חייא's teaching from the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי חייא in step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two sides of a מחלוקת (תנאי היא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed רב and רבי חייא contradict each other, so one of them must be wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are correct. רב follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, and רבי חייא follows the רבנן.

steps.title: רבא begins quoting the משנה where the argument appears
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts bringing the משנה that shows the argument between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן, which opens with a case of three לוגין of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: three לוגין of water...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא begins quoting the משנה that proves his answer, and the quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא needs to show that this argument between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן really exists. So he points to a משנה about three לוגין of drawn water. Only the opening words appear here; the details of the case and the two opinions come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic teaching of the תנאים that the גמרא builds on
Three לוגין, the amount of drawn water that can disqualify a מקוה
Drawn water, water poured by hand or from a vessel; too much of it disqualifies a מקוה

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Three log of water
phrases.notes: This is drawn water. The משנה keeps going after this, and the rest of the case comes next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source behind רבא's claim in step 27 that רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן argue about this.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that רבי יוחנן בן נורי and the רבנן argue about wine-colored water in a מקוה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (מקואות 7:5) about three לוגין of drawn water. It is only begun here and continues next.
